entries.title: Getting started
text: This guide covers DNV turrets, tanks, weapons, ships, aircraft and strategic sites. Click blue contents links to jump; use book corners to turn pages. For DNV 1.20hotfix. The Chinese edition is in the same creative tab.
Prepare a deployer, matching ammo and power, then choose clear ground. Check current recipes for crafting and assembly. Creative items do not always have survival recipes.
Values describe defaults. Server settings, armor and protection can change results. Practice away from buildings.

entries.title: Controls
text: Vehicles use SBW controls. Open the Superb Warfare and DNV sections in Controls to rebind them. These labels show your current keys.
Fire: [[key.superbwarfare.fire]]
Reload: [[key.superbwarfare.reload]]
Vehicle interact: [[key.superbwarfare.interact]]
Dismount: [[key.superbwarfare.dismount]]
Next ammo type: [[key.superbwarfare.change_ammo_forward]]
Blizzard mode: [[key.doggiesnewvehicle.blizzard_mode]]
Check the selected weapon, ammo, reload and energy. Changing ammo is separate from changing weapons.

entries.title: Ammo and power
text: Load the matching SBW ammunition shown by the vehicle inventory, reticle or missing-ammo message. AP suits armor; HE provides blast damage against lighter targets.
Energy weapons need FE. Use a charged compatible battery in the inventory or supported power equipment. Actual charging also depends on the source output.
Activate automatic turrets and remote heavy guns. The three light AA guns use seated control and need neither activation nor FE. Batteries cannot replace ammunition.

entries.title: Twin Bofors
text: A twin light AA gun for low aircraft and light targets. It has two seats; use the gunner seat to aim and fire.
Its magazine holds 32 rounds. Load matching small-caliber ammunition and choose AP or HE. Shells take time to travel: lead moving targets.
AP does not break terrain. HE still has a small blast, so watch nearby allies. Keep a clear muzzle and an open firing lane.

entries.title: Quad Bofors
text: Four barrels provide dense fire across low flight paths. The 64-round magazine supports sustained bursts, but consumes ammunition quickly.
Enter the gunner seat, check ammo type and lead moving targets. AP suits harder targets; HE can damage nearby light targets.
AP leaves terrain intact. This fixed gun needs cover at its flanks and during reloads. A large volume of fire still needs accurate aim.

entries.title: Flak38
text: A quad-barrel light AA gun with one gunner seat and an 80-round magazine. It can track light air or ground targets from a fixed position.
Load the small-caliber shells named by the HUD, enter the seat and use the cross sight. Check muzzle clearance at close range and lead distant moving targets.
AP does not break blocks. HE combines direct hits with a small blast. Protect the gun from direct tank fire.

entries.title: Remote guns
text: Flak88, Flak40 and M1 use a Remote Weapon Station. Load the gun itself, supply FE and activate it. Empty-hand right-click on the gun opens its inventory.

Hold the station and right-click your gun within 8 blocks to bind it. Place the station, then right-click it with your main hand. Gun and station must be loaded, in one dimension and within 128 blocks; stay within 8 blocks of the station.
Your body remains beside the station and can be hurt. Keep safe standing space. Occupancy, ownership or a broken link can prevent control.

entries.title: Flak88
text: An 88 mm heavy gun for prepared positions and harder targets. Control it from a Remote Weapon Station, rather than boarding it like a light AA gun.
Load the named ammo, charge and activate the gun. Choose an open firing lane and use aiming feedback to correct each shot while it reloads.
Protect both the station and its supply route. Very close targets or obstructing terrain may require a different position.

entries.title: Flak40
text: A twin 128 mm heavy gun for strong defensive positions and distant hard targets. Bind a station, supply FE, activate and load the gun inventory.
Two barrels do not remove reload limits. Watch reload progress and ammunition use. Account for target movement and shell flight time.
Keep both gun and station clear. When empty, load the gun itself with the ammo named by its message; putting ammo near the station is not enough.

entries.title: M1 Heavy Gun
text: M1 provides heavy fire support through a Remote Weapon Station. It needs activation, FE and matching ammunition.
Aim is limited to about 60 degrees left or right of its base direction, and elevation from -5 to 60 degrees. Face the expected battle area when deploying.
Turning consumes energy; holding still does not incur that aiming cost. Use an indicator to designate a target or trigger a single shot with a crowbar.

entries.title: Storm
text: Storm is a rapid automatic defense turret for approach lanes and groups of light targets. Supply power and activate it with a clear field of view.
Each shot costs 2,500 FE, with a small extra cost when first acquiring a target. Capacity is 2 million FE; sustained combat needs steady charging.
It requires visible targets. Place its muzzle above cover and combine overlapping fields of fire to reduce blind spots.

entries.title: Changfeng
text: Changfeng supplies heavier automatic fire against major threats. Charge and activate it, with an unobstructed line to targets.
Capacity is 2 million FE. Each shot costs 60,000 FE, plus a small initial target-acquisition cost. Watch reserves during long fights.
Give it a broad firing lane instead of a narrow window. Team relations and protection affect which targets are eligible.

entries.title: Jingzhe
text: Jingzhe attacks from above, useful against enemies behind side cover with an exposed roof. Supply energy and activate it.
It can select targets behind walls, but needs at least 3 clear blocks above the target. A sealed roof limits its effect; target selection does not mean all buildings can be penetrated.
Capacity is 5 million FE. Each module prepays 90,000 FE to reload. Other weapons should cover its firing gaps.

entries.title: Apocalypse
text: A heavy tank with 1,800 health, twin main guns, side rockets and guided missiles. Load ammo for each weapon and replenish energy before boarding.
The main guns alternate one shot at a time, with an 8-second reload. Choose AP or HE for the target. Weapons keep their own reloads when switched.
Rockets add pressure; guided missiles need a lock. Retreat behind cover while reloading. High health does not remove the danger of concentrated fire.
Ammo changes affect later loading, not shells already loaded. Check the current weapon and ammunition on the HUD.

entries.title: Project 612
text: A 650-health superheavy tank destroyer with thick armor, a powerful AP shot and slow movement. It currently has no survival recipe.
The gun deals 560 base direct damage with high penetration and an extra health-based component. Reload takes 8 seconds. Use covered anti-armor positions and guard your flanks.
There is no separate horizontal turret traverse: turn the hull to aim. Elevation is about -3 to 25 degrees. Speed is about 3 blocks/s forward and 1 in reverse.

entries.title: Blizzard
text: A 600-health electric hover tank holding 2 million FE. Mode one combines mobility with rapid cold bolts for light targets; each shot costs 3,000 FE.
Hovering and movement also use energy. A jump costs 100,000 FE and has a cooldown. Check overhead clearance and leave enough power to return.

The TV missile is a separate weapon. Firing moves your view to the missile while the tank stops. Your body stays in the vehicle. Exit control or impact restores the view; a surviving released missile continues forward.
Cold damage depends on target armor. Check the HUD before changing weapons or modes.

entries.title: Charged beam
text: Switch Blizzard to mode two on solid ground, then wait about 1 second for the hatch to deploy. Liquid surfaces cannot support firing readiness.
Hold fire for 3 seconds to shoot one penetrating beam, up to 80 blocks. It costs 75,000 FE, then cools for 2 seconds. Holding fire starts another cycle.
Damage is applied along the path at the instant of firing, once per target. It passes through entities but stops at obstructing terrain. Turning afterward does not sweep new damage.
The blue bar fills upward; red drains during cooldown. Release early to let charge fade slowly, or hold again to resume. Leaving the seat or changing weapon clears charge.

entries.title: HexBot
text: An unarmed six-legged walker for travel and observation. It needs no fuel. Board and use normal vehicle movement controls; target horizontal speed is about 5 blocks/s.
Its feet adapt to the ground and the body can step over local obstacles where there is room. High walls, low ceilings, missing footing and unloaded edges stop progress.
It cannot climb every wall and has no hidden gun. Leave space for the body and all six legs; choose another route when blocked.

entries.title: Allied AI tank
text: The allied AI Apocalypse is a separate unmanned guard tank, with no seats or survival recipe. Deployment inherits your team; it patrols near its anchor and engages explicit enemies.
It shares the player tank's 1,800 health and weapon system, but drives and aims automatically. Leave room for its full hull and travel path.
It ignores players, allies and neutral creatures. Stray shots can still hurt them. It loses hidden targets. Cannon, rockets and missiles fire after aligning.

entries.title: Silo deployment
text: A nuclear silo is a costly strategic site. Only one nuclear or Dog Egg site can occupy a dimension. Bring the deployer, a physical missile and 20 million FE; deployment grants no free payload or power.
Clearance is 17 by 17 blocks, 11 above and 10 below. The central 9 by 9 area is excavated. Remove entities, containers and protected obstructions; keep chunks and the launch opening clear.
The silo has 800 health. Destruction with a nuclear missile inside may cause a detonation. Keep it away from homes and stores.
Normal recovery preserves inventory and energy. Remote deployment still needs ownership and valid clearance.

entries.title: Nuclear launch
text: Normal preparation after loading takes 5 minutes. The final warning does not permit early fire. Once ready, submit a target using the native indicator, or a tactical terminal with an offhand indicator.
Arms retract and the path is checked. Launch uses one missile and 20M FE. Rejection messages list time, charge, target, clearance or owner issues.
Maximum target distance is 200,000 blocks. Accepted missiles fly independently; you need not keep guiding. A missile has 500 health and can be intercepted.
Creative readiness tools advance eligible preparation only; they do not supply ammo or power.

entries.title: Nuclear impact
text: Entity effects extend far beyond the crater: default outer blast radius is 112 blocks, radiation 48. The crater edge is not a safe distance.
The crater combines a radius-16 central sphere with a shallow radius-40 outer footprint, reaching 8 down and 20 up. The center is deeper while the surface coverage is wider.
As the blast spreads, blocks and fluids disappear and the ground can catch fire. Keep moving away when the smoke column rises.
Protection, unbreakable blocks and mobGriefing limit terrain damage. Residual fire expires; entity damage and radiation have separate rules.

entries.title: Dog Egg silo
text: This site uses its own Vacuum Dog Egg ammunition, not nuclear missiles. Deployment, power, preparation and indicator controls follow the nuclear silo, and share its one-site dimension limit.
Impact first pulls eligible enemies and some empty neutral vehicles within 32 blocks, then shows the large dog and detonates. The main strike is concentrated within 12 to 16 blocks.
Ordinary terrain is pulled from a radius-16 sphere in batches. Protection, containers, fluids and highly resistant blocks restrict removal. Neutral vehicles can be pulled without being executed.
The core needs wild dog milk. Use an empty milk carton on a living wolf; crafting returns the empty carton.

entries.title: Helmsman DSX1
text: A bolt-action sniper weapon with a 5-round magazine and adjustable 4x to 8x scope. Bring matching ammunition for distant observation and precise fire.
Aim, fire and reload use normal SBW gun controls. Each shot needs a bolt cycle. You can reload and cycle the bolt while scoped, but cannot fire like an automatic rifle.
Use cover with a retreat route, and adjust aim using range and magnification. Close enemies exploit the narrow scoped view and the gap between shots.

entries.title: Libertad battleship
text: 80M FE. Research a plan with a legendary material pack, paper and cannon core. Assemble 32 hull sections, 2 propulsion sections, 1 armament assembly, 8 intelligent chips and the plan.
Allow 150 blocks of open water. One per dimension. Mode 1: helm fires main guns. With ammo and power, toggle secondaries: [[key.libertad.secondaries]]

32 knots on calm water. Mode 1 side seats: frame, lock, return [[key.libertad.watch_camera]] Orbit with mouse, zoom with wheel, move focus along deck with Ctrl+wheel. Mode 2: fire your side. Carry ammo.
Toggle automatic secondaries from the helm in Mode 1. Wait out a mode cooldown and recharge the ship if close-in defense reports low power.

entries.title: Yue-class carrier
text: 160M FE. Research a plan with a legendary material pack, paper and large propeller. Assemble 24 hull sections, 4 propulsion sections, 8 flight decks, 16 intelligent chips and the plan.
Crafted carriers have 3 empty bays. Insert Feiying crates. Up to 2 can fly at once. Open the panel: [[key.dnvcarriercube.panel]]

Lock the deck. Board from a stocked bay. With lift stopped, pilot seated and bow clear, launch. Charge for 10 seconds. Once all riders leave, sneak-use a crowbar to pack the ship, even in hover. Place the crate elsewhere and open it with the crowbar.
Deck won't lock? Stop cruise or warp. Finish deck work and clear obstructions or move to loaded open space. At 0 health, blast effects mark the start of the fall.

entries.title: Feiying flight
text: Build with 8 steel blocks, 1 heavy armament module, 1 large battery pack, 2 large motors, 2 large propellers and 3 wheels.
Jet / hover mode: [[key.dnvcarriercube.flight_mode]]

A/D roll in jet mode or turn in hover. Slot 2 holds four special missiles. Reload with large anti-ground missiles. Both modes lock visible air and ground enemies at any height. Switching to cannon keeps loaded rounds. Missiles self-destruct on loss of target.
Request recovery: [[key.dnvcarriercube.return_to_carrier]]

Stop on deck and stow in the original bay. An occupied helm confirms. A destroyed deck fighter leaves a wreck. Refill its bay with a new crate. Off deck, sneak-use a crowbar on an empty jet in either mode.

entries.title: Other encounters
text: Noise, CUBE, Heaven and the hostile mothership are special combat content. Their controllers are not ordinary survival tank blueprints; access and team behavior differ from player vehicles.
Against large threats, find cover and an escape route before dividing anti-armor and air-defense roles. Heavy weapons and blasts may still hit allies.
Route platforms and management tools serve specific map scenarios. Ordinary guns and tanks do not require a route or crew core: follow their chapters directly.

entries.title: Troubleshooting
text: Cannot fire: check weapon, ammo type, inventory, reload, FE, activation, seat authority and firing limits. Remote guns take ammo in the gun, not the station.
Cannot deploy: check ground support, full clearance, entity overlap, protection, loaded chunks and site limits. Nuclear sites also need an open launch path, preparation and a valid target.
No terrain damage: check mobGriefing and protection. Light AA AP intentionally preserves blocks. Automatic guns generally need visible targets.
